own_solution.law: Conservation of momentum gives the rocket equation: v = u ln(mi/mf). For initial payload mass P in kg, v = 3 ln((3200 + P)/(800 + P)) km/s.
assumptions: Classical rocket mechanics applies at these speeds.
Exhaust speed is constant relative to the rocket, and external forces are negligible.
The numerical base answer assumes no payload aboard; the problem does not explicitly state this.
A payload attached to the rocket remains aboard throughout the burn.

defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: The base specifies body-and-engine mass and fuel mass but does not state whether an initial payload is aboard, so the total initial and final masses are not uniquely determined.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T357D and T23F7 replace the specified 190 kg payload with an unspecified 'small payload', so the payload variants do not all preserve the same stated number and unit.

counterexamples.case: The base rocket also carries a 190 kg payload throughout the burn.
counterexamples.result: Its empty body-and-engine mass remains 800 kg and its fuel mass remains 2400 kg, but its final speed is 3 ln(3390/990) = 3.692640772 km/s rather than 4.158883083 km/s.

notes: All numerical assignments assume that no payload is aboard except one explicitly attached to the rocket by the added sentence. The relevant-payload calculations also assume that the stated payload is the entire payload. At 27 kg/s the burn lasts 2400/27 = 88.8889 s; the rate enters thrust and mass depletion but cancels from the integrated velocity change. The nearby tug has no appreciable interaction with the rocket under the stated external-force condition. T5A37, T5460, T3A6F and T2E45 preserve 190 kg; T357D and T23F7 omit that value. The two fuel-rate sentences both preserve 27 kg/s.
